name: Automated Lead Generation
desc: Automated Reddit lead generation system using RSS feeds and adaptive API requests to minimize rate limits and enable lightweight background monitoring.
challenge: The main hurdle with building an automated lead generation system with reddit is its aapi. Reddit is notorious for rate limiting and banning people who are utilizing the api too much. Thus, a system needed to be created that is both highly efficient and light weight to run in background
approach: My main focus with this project was to bypass the reddit API restrictions and rate limiting. Therefor, I used RSS feeds with an adaptive listener to send requests to the API in such a way that all the operational needs were met.

metrics.label: Action Friction
metrics.sub: One-click outreach from incoming lead notifications

metrics.label: API Request Reduction
metrics.sub: Using RSS feeds and adaptive request scheduling

process.title: Discovery
process.desc: The Reddit API had restrictions imposed on it around mid 2023, making me choose RSS feeds to avoid rate limiting. Tools to easily access the DB also were made, and the system followed a "one click outreach" philosophy.

process.title: Design
process.desc: To bypass rate limiting, I adopted smart polling which automatically speeds up based on user activity. Both async and sync technologies were used to meet operational requirements. I also adopted a multi layered post filtering strategy. I used discord as a frontend for its convenience.

process.title: Implementation
process.desc: Due to the restrictions, I used RSS feeds and smart polling. Each subreddit is polled on its designated time based on user activity. Async is used to avoid delays. Keyword match and AI made up the multi layered post filtering strategy. I also made passive post ingestion pipelines to generate valuable reports about the market.

outcome: The project was a great learnign oppurtunity. I solved real world problems with constraints such as rate limiting. I made custom solutions to bypass the challenges and optimized the workflows for better execution. Right now, the system runs 24/7 with minimal overhead, is notifies me in imminently and I do outreach in one click. The system also preserves posts for me to gather inspirations to write self intros in subreddits like r/forhire.

features.label: Adaptive Smart Polling
features.desc: dynamic RSS polling intervals scale based on subreddit activity and rate limits
features.detail: Exponential backoff and jitter algorithms dynamically adjust fetch frequencies across monitored subreddits, minimizing API overhead while guaranteeing real-time post ingestion.

features.label: Strategy-Based LLM Integration
features.desc: pluggable LLM provider strategy supporting Gemini, Groq, and local CPU models
features.detail: Hexagonal architecture decoupling domain logic from inference APIs. Features strict JSON schema enforcement via Pydantic and zero-shot intent extraction for high-confidence lead scoring.

features.label: Multi-Layered Filter Pipeline
features.desc: cascading two-stage filter drops non-leads locally before hitting LLM endpoints
features.detail: Combines fast regex pattern matching, post metadata rules (flairs/stickies), and ultra-lightweight local CPU classifiers (DeBERTa/Qwen) to eliminate 85%+ of non-hiring posts with zero API token cost.

features.label: Passive Post Ingestion
features.desc: non-blocking background worker stream continuously capturing incoming leads
features.detail: Asynchronous RSS feed ingestion engine featuring post deduplication, title/body truncation guards, and automated state tracking to handle high-frequency feed updates smoothly.

features.label: Database Debug & Access Suite
features.desc: built-in developer tooling for real-time lead inspection, schema migrations, and queries
features.detail: CLI and administrative utilities providing direct access to lead qualification states, raw LLM JSON outputs, database health metrics, and pipeline debugging logs.

features.label: Resilient Fallback & Circuit Breaker
features.desc: automatic API failover and rate-limit mitigation across multiple provider backends
features.detail: Gracefully handles API rate limits, 400/404 errors, and network timeouts by automatically routing requests to backup LLM models or falling back to local heuristic classifiers.

name: CRSOM
desc: A project for BZU event CRSOM with complex forms and relaible delivery. It was the first digital solution for CRSOM and inlcudes data exporting pipelines.
challenge: The main challenge was building a registration system around the tournament’s specific rules, including limiting each game to a defined number of players while supporting multiple students and mentors. The system also had to handle dynamic fee calculations, image uploads, validation, and registration updates without making the process difficult to use.
approach: With only 7 days to build, I focused on making the complex registration form reliable and intuitive. I implemented the tournament’s rules, dynamic player and mentor management, fee calculations, image compression, API integration, and comprehensive error handling to ensure invalid submissions and edge cases were handled gracefully.

process.title: Discovery
process.desc: Worked with the BZU event organizers to understand the registration requirements, tournament rules, and how the website should look and function.

process.title: Design
process.desc: Designed the interface around the organizers’ requirements, iterating frequently as they refined and changed the design throughout development. I also focused on making the complex, data-heavy registration form usable on mobile.

process.title: Implementation
process.desc: Built the website and registration system with a secure REST API architecture, input validation, error handling, and responsive forms. I then integrated the remaining pages and functionality into a complete, production-ready website.

outcome: CRSOM was a huge success. More participants registered than in all previous years thanks to a single digital portal where everyone could gather information and register. The whole project was made on a time squeeze of just 7 days. I learned about working in high stress enviroments, making complex and dynamic forms that differed from the industries usual challenges and architectured a new solution for it

features.label: Dynamic Complex Forms
features.desc: Built dynamic registration forms with state-dependent fields, dynamic array rendering, and custom Joi validation message formatting.
features.detail: Implemented conditional validation rules and dynamic array mappings for student and mentor entries where input requirements update dynamically based on user selections.

features.label: Automated Excel Data Export
features.desc: Developed a dedicated backend route allowing external spreadsheets and admin tools to scrape or ingest live registration data automatically.
features.detail: Built an automated data endpoint that parses and formats raw database entries into structured formats optimized for Excel ingestion, reporting, and admin workflows.

features.label: Real-time Team Validation Engine
features.desc: Enforced complex game logic and player capacities dynamically before form submission.
features.detail: Created custom middleware validation to strictly enforce rules such as Game 4's exact 4 or 8 total player splits and Game 5's max team thresholds.

features.label: Multi-Entity Duplicate Protection
features.desc: Integrated database uniqueness checks for multiple fields across nested document arrays.
features.detail: Implemented asynchronous MongoDB queries checking for globally unique WhatsApp numbers, student CNICs, teacher contact numbers, and single-submission user IDs.

features.label: Human-Readable Error Normalization
features.desc: Transformed raw backend/Joi validation errors into user-friendly error strings.
features.detail: Built a custom error parser that converts 0-indexed schema error messages into 1-indexed mentor/student labels with readable alternative options.

name: Twitter REST API
desc: Twitter-like REST API focused on scalable backend architecture, asynchronous background processing, and fast data access through Redis caching.
challenge: I wanted to create something more than a basic Twitter clone. The main challenge was designing the architecture behind a large REST API while keeping it fast and responsive. It needed to handle frequent operations such as fetching tweets and view counts without repeatedly hitting the database. The system also needed background processing for tasks that did not need to block API requests.
approach: My main focus with this project was the backend architecture rather than simply adding endpoints. I used Redis as a caching layer so frequently requested data could be returned without querying PostgreSQL every time. Celery handles background processes such as syncing view counts from the cache back into the database, keeping those operations away from the main request cycle.

metrics.label: Non critical tasks offloaded
metrics.sub: Using celery non critical tasks such as views counting were cached and scheduled for later

metrics.label: Reduced DB operations.
metrics.sub: By implementing caching (Redis) many request hit cache instead of the DB.

metrics.label: API enpoints
metrics.sub: Structered for 6 core domains (Auth, Users, Tweets, Replies, Lists, Bookmarks).

process.title: Architecture
process.desc: I first broke the application into its main resources: users, tweets, replies, bookmarks, and lists. Each resource needed its own CRUD operations where appropriate, while authentication was kept separate. The goal was to make the API large without making the architecture difficult to maintain.

process.title: Performance
process.desc: A Twitter-like application constantly reads data, so hitting PostgreSQL for every request would create unnecessary overhead. I added Redis as a caching layer and designed the API to return cached data when available. Celery was then introduced for operations that could safely happen in the background.

process.title: Implementation
process.desc: I implemented more than 36 endpoints across the main API resources, backed by PostgreSQL. Redis handles frequently accessed data while Celery processes background jobs such as syncing cached view counts into the database. The result is an API where the request cycle stays focused on returning a response instead of doing every operation synchronously.

outcome: This project taught me how much of backend development is really about architecture. Building the endpoints was only one part of it. I had to think about where data should live, when it should be cached, and which operations should happen outside the request cycle. The final API has more than 36 endpoints, uses Redis for fast reads, PostgreSQL as the primary database, and Celery for background processing.

features.label: Celery Background Processing
features.desc: background workers handle operations that do not need to block API responses
features.detail: Celery workers process asynchronous tasks such as syncing tweet view counts from Redis back into PostgreSQL, keeping slower operations outside the main request cycle.

features.label: Built-In Redis Caching
features.desc: cached results are returned directly when available
features.detail: The API checks Redis before querying PostgreSQL for cacheable data. This reduces repeated database reads and keeps frequently accessed resources fast.

features.label: Resource-Based REST API
features.desc: 36+ endpoints organized around the application's core resources
features.detail: The API is structured around authentication, users, tweets, replies, bookmarks, and lists, with CRUD operations where they make sense for each resource.

features.label: Tweet & Reply System
features.desc: complete API support for creating and managing tweets and replies
features.detail: Tweet and reply resources support the operations required to create, retrieve, update, and delete content while keeping their relationships manageable through the API.

features.label: Bookmark Management
features.desc: lightweight bookmark creation and removal without unnecessary CRUD operations
features.detail: Bookmarks use a focused resource design where only the operations that make sense for the feature are exposed instead of forcing a generic CRUD structure.

features.label: List Management
features.desc: full CRUD support for user-created Twitter-style lists
features.detail: Users can create, retrieve, update, and delete lists through dedicated API endpoints, with the architecture leaving room for managing list membership separately.

name: Dotfiles
desc: Modular Arch Linux configuration built around GNU tools, custom window management, a tailored development environment, and lightweight system automation.
challenge: The main challenge with maintaining a Linux setup is keeping everything consistent without turning the configuration into a collection of random tweaks. I wanted the system to stay modular, easy to understand, and lightweight. Every part of the desktop had to serve a purpose, while custom scripts and services needed to work together without adding unnecessary overhead.
approach: My main focus with this project was the architecture of the system rather than its appearance. I chose GNU tools because of their simplicity and modularity, then structured the configuration so individual components could be changed without affecting the rest of the setup. Hyprland handles the current Wayland desktop while my previous Qtile and X11 configuration is still maintained. Around it, I built a consistent development workflow, custom utilities, and lightweight desktop services.

metrics.label: Idle CPU Reduction
metrics.sub: Optimized moving wallpapers from roughly 20% idle CPU usage to 10%

metrics.label: Display Architectures
metrics.sub: Maintains both the current Wayland setup and previous X11 configuration

metrics.label: Custom Workflow
metrics.sub: Development, desktop, browser, and system utilities configured around a single workflow

process.title: Architecture
process.desc: I started with modularity as the main principle. GNU utilities made it easy to keep individual pieces of the system separate and predictable. Instead of relying on one large configuration, each component has its own configuration and can be changed independently.

process.title: Desktop
process.desc: The desktop evolved from Qtile and X11 into my current Hyprland and Wayland setup. I configured Waybar, Rofi, and SwayNC around the workflow I actually use, including a custom Rofi theme and notification setup. The older X11 configuration remains available rather than being discarded.

process.title: Optimization
process.desc: System scripts handle repetitive tasks such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, screenshots, and window capture. I also experimented with moving wallpapers, but the initial version used too much CPU while idle. I slowed and simplified the rendering until I found a version that kept the effect without wasting resources, cutting idle CPU usage from around 20% to 10%.

outcome: This project became less about customizing Linux and more about designing a system that behaves exactly how I expect it to. The configuration is modular, portable, and easy to modify when my workflow changes. My development environment, desktop, browser, and system utilities all follow the same philosophy: keep things simple, remove unnecessary overhead, and automate the repetitive parts.

features.label: Modular Configuration Architecture
features.desc: separate system configurations built around simple, composable GNU tools
features.detail: The dotfiles are organized by application and responsibility, allowing individual components to be changed, replaced, or restored without restructuring the entire system.

features.label: Wayland Desktop Environment
features.desc: Hyprland setup with custom window management, notifications, panels, and application launcher
features.detail: Hyprland provides the current window management layer, with Waybar, Rofi, and SwayNC configured to fit the same workflow. Previous Qtile and X11 configurations are also preserved.

features.label: Integrated Development Workflow
features.desc: Neovim and terminal tooling configured around a consistent development workflow
features.detail: Neovim was configured from scratch with custom keybindings, language tooling, navigation, completion, formatting, and project workflows. Tmux provides persistent multi-terminal sessions without relying on a graphical terminal layout.

features.label: System Automation Scripts
features.desc: small shell utilities for common desktop and system operations
features.detail: Custom scripts simplify Wi-Fi and Bluetooth control, screenshots, window capture, and screen selection. Repetitive system actions become single commands instead of manual sequences.

features.label: Performance-Focused Desktop
features.desc: system effects tuned around resource usage rather than visual effects alone
features.detail: Moving wallpapers were initially too expensive to run continuously, consuming around 20% CPU while idle. The rendering speed and workload were reduced until the same idea could run at roughly half the idle CPU usage.

features.label: Minimal Browser Environment
features.desc: Firefox interface redesigned around a clean and distraction-free workflow
features.detail: Custom userChrome.css and userContent.css configurations control the browser's interface and page presentation, keeping Firefox visually consistent with the rest of the desktop.
